sections.subtitle: Glass was split into Architectural Glass and Automotive, and Life Science carved out of Chemicals, from FY2022 -- series before and after that line are not the same businesses

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For AGC Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For AGC Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For AGC Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For AGC Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For AGC Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For AGC Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For AGC Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For AGC Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For AGC Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

segmentRevenue.title: Revenue by segment
segmentRevenue.content:
AGC reports revenue across five segments: Architectural Glass (float/building glass, Japan and overseas), Automotive (OEM windshields and glazing), Electronics (display glass and semiconductor/optoelectronic materials), Chemicals (chlor-alkali/essential chemicals plus performance fluorochemicals) and Life Science (biopharma/small-molecule CDMO).

For AGC Inc.: the single Glass segment reported through FY2021 was split into Architectural Glass and Automotive from FY2022 (restated FY2023), and Life Science was carved out of Chemicals the same year -- so Glass and its two successor series never overlap, and comparing a pre-2022 bar to a post-2022 bar across that line mixes two different segment definitions.

What to watch:

  • Electronics and Life Science (the higher-growth, higher-margin "strategic" businesses) rising as a share of the mix
  • Architectural Glass's slow decline against the stable, cyclical Automotive and Chemicals base

segmentOperatingIncome.title: Operating income by segment
segmentOperatingIncome.content:
The same five-segment split (plus Ceramics/Other) as the revenue chart, but for operating income -- which segments actually make money, not just sales.

For AGC Inc.: Life Science has posted an operating loss every year since it was split out in FY2022 (JPY -22.3bn in FY2025) as the CDMO business builds out capacity ahead of revenue; Automotive and Electronics swing with auto production and the semiconductor cycle, while Chemicals' FY2021-22 spike reflects an unusually strong chlor-alkali pricing environment that has since normalised.

What to watch:

  • Whether Life Science losses are narrowing as CDMO contracts scale
  • Chemicals operating income reverting further toward its pre-FY2021 range
  • Architectural Glass margin under pressure from a shrinking top line

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For AGC Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
